responses.leak_example: days_past_due_60 and collection_calls are recorded after the application, when the customer has already started missing payments, so the bank cannot know them at decision time and they almost reveal default_within_90d. Keeping them gave a fake AP of 0.999 and ROC-AUC of 0.9999, so I dropped both before training.
responses.split_reason: The real model scores future applicants it has never seen, so each fold trains on the past and validates on a later 6-month window. Training rows are kept only if their 90-day label was known before validation starts, and customers in the validation window are purged from training, so no fold shares a customer (0 shared). Tuning used a separate reserved pool of 1,935 early rows, so the outer folds stay untouched.
responses.observed_gap: Leaky random minus clean random was +0.688 AP (0.999 vs 0.311), so leakage was the main source of fake performance. Clean random minus honest fixed was -0.004 AP (0.311 vs 0.315), smaller than the fold SD of about 0.03-0.04, so the customer overlap did not clearly inflate scores here. The tuned model (AP 0.313, ROC-AUC 0.786) did not beat the fixed 80-tree baseline (AP 0.315, ROC-AUC 0.798).
responses.imputer_reason: The imputer must be fitted on the training rows of each fold only, then applied to validation. If it learned medians from all rows, information from validation or future applications would leak into training and make the scores optimistic. At decision time the bank only has past data to fill missing values.
responses.limitations: Only 3 outer folds with about 110-139 defaults each, so the SD is not a confidence interval and differences under 0.03 AP may be noise. The setups use different populations (10,000 vs 5,039 rows), and 49.6% of rows have no honest prediction. The search was small (8 trials, FAST_MODE) and its last inner fold had only 15 defaults. The data is synthetic, and calibration was not checked.
